revision_notes: Revision 3 addresses reviewer_plan NACK 3994da6c on rev 2. Two blocking items + five non-blocking items resolved against verified code. (a) BLOCKING #1 — RISK-3 + DEP-4 rewritten from 'Gunicorn worker starvation' to 'Waitress 16-thread starvation'. Orchestrator uses `waitress.serve(app, host=host, port=port, threads=16)` at orchestrator/cli.py:288-290 (verified). There is no Gunicorn, no gunicorn.conf.py, no `worker_class` anywhere in orchestrator/ or k8s/. Mitigation now targets a new `EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS` env var with `default=max(16, max_concurrent_long_polls + 4)`, drops the 'switch to gevent/eventlet' recommendation (Waitress already accommodates blocking I/O), drops the 'Gunicorn --timeout 2×cap' point (Waitress has no per-request timeout equivalent — its channel_timeout defaults to 120s and applies to idle HTTP channels, not request handlers). Affected components corrected to orchestrator/cli.py:288-290 and a new env-loader location. This forces a parallel correction in plan TASK-4-1 (currently references gunicorn.conf.py / gevent / worker_class) and the architect Track 7 rationale — coordination flagged to task_planner and architect. (b) BLOCKING #2 — RISK-4 + DEP-3 rewritten. Squid timeouts are hardcoded at gateway/squid.conf:135-137 (`connect_timeout 30`, `read_timeout 60`, `request_timeout 60`), NOT exposed as a ConfigMap key. The 'raise the Squid ConfigMap key' mitigation cannot be satisfied by any operator. Revised mitigation offers two concrete paths: (Path A) add new ConfigMap key (e.g. `gateway-squid-config`) read at gateway container start to template read_timeout/request_timeout into squid.conf; OR (Path B) treat it as an image-rebuild-only knob, cap `EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT` in code at `min(env_value, _SQUID_READ_TIMEOUT_HARDCODED=60)`, and convert the startup WARNING into a refusal-to-boot when env exceeds hardcoded cap. DEP-3 status upgraded from 'ENVIRONMENTAL — not code' to 'ENVIRONMENTAL — baked into image; no runtime affordance'. (c) Non-blocking items added as flagged: DEP-2 residual note on unmitigated connection-pool sizing (plan has no TASK adding `max_connections` to redis-py or sizing pool); RISK-2 residual note on HEARTBEAT rate-limit (architect TD-3 had 429 rate-limit; plan TASK-3-1 dropped it, now classified deferred residual); RISK-7 SSE path is now locked (plan Phase 5 / TASK-5-1) so the 'If SSE path chosen' conditional is dropped and a concrete sandbox SIGTERM test pointer is inserted; open_questions Q3 (exit-code contract) and Q5 (warn on raised cap) marked resolved with task pointers; testing_recommendations load-test scaled down to align with plan TASK-4-1 smoketest (10 sockets) and the 50-socket peak flagged as a follow-up issue; security_posture_summary gains a side-channel completeness note (wait --for HEARTBEAT is observable but no worse than short-poll). External research skipped: internal protocol/CLI refactor with no new third-party supply-chain dependencies (gevent is NOT added — see RISK-3 rewrite).
summary: Risk assessment for full-scope Option C: prompt preamble audit + typed `egg-orch message wait` blocking primitive + env-configurable `--wait` cap + in-memory condition-variable blocking + removal of QUESTION message type + new HEARTBEAT message type with structured state field + explicit prompt Don'ts + consensus_wrapper SSE rewrite (per architect rev 3 / plan Phase 5) + agent-wait-patterns.md + single-idiom docs. Pre-mitigation risk MEDIUM-to-HIGH; post-mitigation risk under the CONFIRMED plan (pending reconciliation of TASK-4-1 Waitress correction) is MEDIUM (dominated by prompt regression + deployment-config drift). The biggest correctness traps — all addressed by the CONFIRMED plan after RISK-3/RISK-4 corrections — are: (1) the refine analysis's premise that `QUESTION` is 'only used in test fixtures' is wrong — `QUESTION` is actively advertised in the reviewer lifecycle prompt at orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:6066-6072 and is a member of BRC_HISTORY_TYPES (pipelines.py:4775; test locked at test_brc_history.py:974-985). Plan Phase 7 stages removal in prompt-→-BRC_HISTORY-→-tests-→-enum order so CI stays green at every commit boundary; TASK-7-1 replaces the QUESTION example with a forward-pointer to the follow-up REQUEST/REPLY issue. (2) the new HEARTBEAT message type overlaps the existing PROGRESS-emitted heartbeat timer in orchestrator/health_monitor.py — plan TASK-3-3 wires an additive MESSAGE_SENT subscription that resets last_heartbeat on message_type==HEARTBEAT, keeps the legacy PROGRESS path behind a TODO, and tests all three paths (HEARTBEAT-only, PROGRESS-only, neither). (3) HTTP_PROXY / Squid timeout coupling has NO ConfigMap affordance — timeouts are hardcoded in the gateway image at gateway/squid.conf:135-137 (`read_timeout 60`, `request_timeout 60`). The plan's TASK-2-3 warning must be either (A) paired with a new ConfigMap key that the gateway entrypoint templates into squid.conf at container start, or (B) downgraded to a hard-cap-in-code + refusal-to-boot when `EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT > _SQUID_READ_TIMEOUT_HARDCODED=60`. (4) condition-variable blocking on the in-memory store must integrate with MessageStore.clear() at phase transitions — plan TASK-1-1 uses a per-pipeline threading.Condition, calls notify_all on clear(), and re-checks `pipeline_id in self._messages` after each wake-up (returns empty list if the pipeline has been cleared). (5) WSGI worker starvation — orchestrator runs Waitress with `threads=16` at orchestrator/cli.py:288-290 (NOT Gunicorn). 30-70 concurrent long-polls saturate at ~16 immediately. Plan Phase 4 must be reconciled (see RISK-3): raise threads via a new `EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS` env var (default `max(16, concurrent_long_polls + 4)`), add a dedicated `/healthz` route that does NOT touch MessageStore, and export an `egg_inflight_long_polls` gauge. Lower-risk concerns addressed: SIGTERM (locked to SSE + curl --no-buffer via RISK-7 mitigation; conditional dropped), prompt regression (locked to regex assertions in test_pipeline_prompts.py rejecting any `for i in [0-9]` or `sleep [0-9]+` outside the Don'ts block, RISK-8), and QUESTION test churn (locked to staged commit order in Phase 7, RISK-10). External research skipped: internal protocol/CLI refactor with no new third-party supply-chain dependencies.

dependencies.dependency: Redis Streams for XREAD BLOCK long-polling semantics
dependencies.assessment: XREAD BLOCK already powers the existing `--wait` parameter (redis_message_store.py:182-188). The new `message wait --for TYPE` adds server-side filtering on top. Redis is the only event-driven backend; the in-memory fallback needs the condition-variable implementation from decision-4. A latent gap flagged by reviewer: no plan task sizes the redis-py connection pool for the new workload; default `redis.ConnectionPool(max_connections=None)` is unbounded, which is 'safe' until paired with Waitress's 16 threads and can then starve the Redis server instead.
risks: `count=limit * 3` over-read may still fall short if many non-matching messages arrive before the target TYPE, causing the server to loop XREAD calls and burn CPU.
If server-side filtering is implemented as a loop over XREAD BLOCK, each iteration costs a round-trip; under high message volume the loop can degenerate to polling.

Redis connection pool exhaustion: Waitress threads × long-blocked XREADs could exceed the Redis server's `maxclients` (default 10000, but memory-bounded) — more realistically, a leaked connection per worker crash accumulates quickly.
NEW (residual from reviewer non-blocking nb-DEP2): no plan task sizes the connection pool — rev 3 flags this as a gap that the implementer must close or the plan must add a new TASK.
dependencies.mitigation: Plan phase must specify: (1) the server-side filter loop has a hard ceiling (e.g., 10 XREAD iterations per client request before returning empty) so a pathological non-matching stream cannot monopolize a worker; (2) redis_message_store connection pool is explicitly sized — recommend adding a TASK-1-4 (plan-side) that passes `max_connections=max_waitress_threads + slack` to the `redis.ConnectionPool(...)` construction in orchestrator/redis_message_store.py; (3) one unit test per message type and `--from ROLE` filter combination asserts the filter is server-side, not client-side. Residual: if the plan does not land (2), rev 3 classifies this as an UNMITIGATED risk that the implementer must flag at review time.

dependencies.status: ENVIRONMENTAL — baked into gateway image; NO ConfigMap affordance
dependencies.assessment: Verified at gateway/squid.conf:135-137 — the file hardcodes `connect_timeout 30 seconds`, `read_timeout 60 seconds`, `request_timeout 60 seconds`. These directives are NOT surfaced via k8s ConfigMap, env var, or entrypoint template. Checking k8s/base/gateway-deployment.yaml confirms only `PROXY_PORT=3129`, `GATEWAY_PORT`, `HEALTH_PORT`, `GATEWAY_THREADS` (DEFAULT_THREADS=32) are exposed — nothing Squid-timeout-adjacent. This means an operator CANNOT raise the Squid timeouts without rebuilding the gateway image (or shipping a patched squid.conf via volume mount, which is not done today). The rev 2 DEP-3 status ('ENVIRONMENTAL — not code') was underspecified; rev 3 explicitly says 'baked into image, no runtime affordance'.
risks: A deployment applies a ConfigMap raising `EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT=600` without a matching Squid timeout bump → intermittent 504 on long waits indistinguishable from a real orchestrator hang. Today the ONLY way to bump Squid is rebuild the gateway image with a patched squid.conf.
A future gateway image update that tightens squid.conf (e.g., for a security fix) silently breaks all long-poll agents.
Local docker-compose and k3s deployments ship the same gateway image — there is no 'just the dev override' knob.
dependencies.mitigation: See RISK-4 for the two-path resolution (A: add ConfigMap key + entrypoint template; B: hardcode cap in orchestrator code + refusal-to-boot). DEP-3's role is just to state that the 'coupling' is baked-in at image-build time, not runtime. The plan MUST pick A or B and implement the matching task; leaving it as a runbook note (rev 2 wording) is insufficient per reviewer NACK item 2.

dependencies.dependency: Orchestrator WSGI server — Waitress with threads=16
dependencies.status: PRESENT — Waitress 16 threads, audited, undersized for the new workload
dependencies.assessment: Verified at orchestrator/cli.py:288-290: `from waitress import serve; serve(app, host=host, port=port, threads=16)`. The inline comment at cli.py:285-287 states: '16 threads handles concurrent requests including Redis XREAD BLOCK long-polling (capped at 60s per request in messages.py). Waitress thread pool accommodates blocking I/O without requiring async workers.' This is TRUE today because the current `--wait` cap IS 60s and concurrent-long-poll count is low. Once the new `message wait --for TYPE` primitive lands AND agents adopt it at scale (the stated goal of issue #1897), 30-70 simultaneous blocking sockets saturate 16 threads almost immediately. Waitress does NOT need to be replaced — its thread pool handles blocking I/O correctly — it needs to be sized larger. There is no Gunicorn, no gevent, no async worker class anywhere in orchestrator/ or k8s/; rev 2's claim otherwise was incorrect and is corrected here.
risks: Request queueing: short orchestrator API calls (status, signal) get queued behind long waits when threads are saturated, making the whole orchestrator appear hung.

Kubernetes readiness probe: if the probe endpoint competes for the same Waitress thread pool, long waits can cause probe timeouts and a restart storm. (See TASK-4-2 plan correction: /healthz must not touch MessageStore.)

Waitress `channel_timeout` (default 120s) applies to idle HTTP channels, NOT to blocking request handlers — there is no per-request-timeout equivalent to Gunicorn's `--timeout` that would kill a mid-block thread. The rev 2 recommendation 'raise Gunicorn --timeout' was inapplicable.
Thread-pool starvation IS the workload-peak failure mode even without any per-request-timeout fire.
dependencies.mitigation: Plan Phase 4 TASK-4-1 MUST be reconciled from its current Gunicorn/gevent language to Waitress thread-count tuning: (a) introduce a new `EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS` env var consumed at orchestrator/cli.py:288-290, defaulting to `max(16, int(os.environ.get('EGG_MAX_CONCURRENT_LONG_POLLS', '64')) + 4)`; (b) remove all references to `gunicorn.conf.py`, `worker_class`, and `gevent` from plan TASK-4-1 and architect Track 7 — these files and concepts do not exist in this codebase; (c) update the k8s/base/orchestrator-deployment.yaml resource requests only if the threads bump changes memory footprint materially (per thread ≈ 8MB stack default; 64 threads × 8MB = 512MB overhead, within the current 4Gi limit but worth stating); (d) the `/healthz` route added by TASK-4-2 must remain MessageStore-free so probes don't contend for request threads; (e) the `egg_inflight_long_polls` gauge (TASK-4-3) should be paired with a Waitress-thread-in-use gauge (via `waitress.task.Task` instrumentation or a simple counter decorator) so operators can compare the two and diagnose saturation.

dependencies.assessment: health_monitor already tracks `last_heartbeat` per agent as a timestamp, reset on PROGRESS events with `type=heartbeat` (health_monitor.py:248-257). Tier 1 alert fires on `orchestrator_heartbeat_timeout_seconds` (600s in implement phase). The proposed new HEARTBEAT message type is a separate bus-level signal with a structured state field. If the health_monitor's heartbeat timer is NOT wired to also reset on HEARTBEAT-type messages, an agent that emits HEARTBEAT but not PROGRESS-heartbeat will falsely trip Tier 1.
risks: Dual heartbeat systems diverge: agents assume HEARTBEAT message is sufficient and stop emitting PROGRESS-heartbeat, falsely tripping alerts.
Overseer nudges fire on agents that are alive and communicating via the new channel, polluting the bus (re-introducing the exact problem #1897 set out to fix).
Test-only divergence: unit tests of the new HEARTBEAT path pass but integration tests of health_monitor still assert PROGRESS-heartbeat resets.
dependencies.mitigation: Plan phase must explicitly include a task: wire the health_monitor to subscribe to MESSAGE_SENT events with `message_type=HEARTBEAT` and reset `last_heartbeat` on those too. Add an integration test in test_health_monitor.py that: (1) agent sends HEARTBEAT message but no PROGRESS; (2) advance time past heartbeat_timeout; (3) assert no alert fired. Also add a deprecation note that PROGRESS-heartbeat will be retired after HEARTBEAT is universally adopted (do NOT retire in this PR — that's a migration risk).

risks.title: New HEARTBEAT message type creates dual heartbeat systems that can diverge
risks.description: The Tier 1 HealthMonitor (orchestrator/health_monitor.py) already tracks `last_heartbeat` per agent as a timestamp, reset on PROGRESS_EMITTED events where `event.data['type'] == 'heartbeat'` (health_monitor.py:248-257). The `orchestrator_heartbeat_timeout_seconds` threshold (default 120s; 600s in implement phase per lines 165-175) fires heartbeat_timeout alerts if not reset in time (line 451). The issue #1897 resolution of Q4 adds a NEW `HEARTBEAT` message type on the message bus with a structured `state` field. If the HealthMonitor only subscribes to PROGRESS_EMITTED, agents that adopt the new HEARTBEAT and stop emitting progress-heartbeat will falsely trip the Tier 1 alarm — re-introducing the overseer-noise problem the issue set out to fix. Conversely, if the HealthMonitor is wired to BOTH and agents emit both, it's not a bug but duplicate work.
risks.mitigation: (1) Plan task MUST add an explicit MESSAGE_SENT subscription in HealthMonitor that resets `last_heartbeat` when `message_type == 'HEARTBEAT'`. (2) Add a health_monitor integration test that: (a) emits only HEARTBEAT messages (no PROGRESS); (b) advances time past heartbeat_timeout; (c) asserts NO heartbeat_timeout alert raised. (3) Do NOT remove the PROGRESS-heartbeat path in this PR — it remains the legacy path. Document the deprecation in a code comment and a follow-up issue. (4) Define the HEARTBEAT payload schema precisely in the plan: `{state: 'WORKING'|'WAITING_ON_ROLE'|'PROPOSED'|'IDLE', waiting_on?: role, since?: iso-timestamp}` and validate it at `send_message` time (routes/messages.py) so a malformed HEARTBEAT is rejected before it pollutes the bus. (5) RESIDUAL (rev 3, from reviewer non-blocking): architect TD-3 specified a rate limit at send_message (`EGG_HEARTBEAT_RATE_LIMIT` default 20/min, 429 above cap). Plan TASK-3-1 includes schema validation but NOT the rate limit. This is a deferred mitigation: without it, a misbehaving or test-fixture agent can flood the bus with HEARTBEAT messages faster than consumers drain them. The implementer should either add rate-limiting as a follow-up TASK-3-4 or explicitly accept the residual risk with a test that measures observed HEARTBEAT volume against the 20/min target under normal operation.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert the HEARTBEAT enum member and the HealthMonitor subscription. If agents have started emitting HEARTBEAT, revert producer code first (one PR), then revert the type. The overseer fallback to PROGRESS-heartbeat remains intact because we did not remove it.
risks.human_review_reason: Heartbeat semantics cross the message store → EventBus → HealthMonitor boundary. A reviewer should verify the plan wires both heartbeat paths into the same timer, otherwise the Tier 1 overseer will nudge agents that are reporting state correctly via the new channel. The rate-limit residual (mitigation point 5) is an additional ask that needs reviewer sign-off on whether to land it in this PR or defer.

risks.title: Waitress thread pool (16 threads) starvation from 30-70 concurrent long-blocking sockets
risks.description: Verified at orchestrator/cli.py:288-290 — the orchestrator runs under Waitress with `threads=16` (hardcoded). The adjacent comment at lines 285-287 explicitly states this configuration 'handles concurrent requests including Redis XREAD BLOCK long-polling (capped at 60s per request in messages.py). Waitress thread pool accommodates blocking I/O without requiring async workers.' This is true TODAY because long-poll concurrency is low. Once issue #1897's new `message wait --for TYPE` primitive lands and agents adopt it at scale, the refine analysis estimates 30-70 simultaneous long-poll sockets at peak (3-7 agents × 10 concurrent pipelines). 30+ blocking requests against a 16-thread pool = immediate saturation. Short requests (pipeline/status, consensus/signal) queue behind long waits. There is no Gunicorn in this codebase — rev 2's references to Gunicorn `--timeout` and async worker classes (gevent/eventlet) were factually incorrect and are withdrawn. Waitress has a `channel_timeout` (default 120s) that applies to idle HTTP channels, NOT a per-request-handler timeout; there is no equivalent knob to forcibly kill a blocked thread after a configured duration.
affected_components: A new env-var loader (location TBD during implementation, likely near the existing env reads in orchestrator/cli.py or orchestrator/app.py)
k8s/base/orchestrator-deployment.yaml — resource requests/limits, readinessProbe (probe will be re-pointed at /healthz by plan TASK-4-2)
orchestrator/routes/messages.py:164-184 — long-polling code path (the request handler that blocks)
risks.mitigation: (1) Plan Phase 4 / TASK-4-1 MUST be corrected from its current Gunicorn/gevent language to Waitress thread-count tuning. Introduce a new `EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS` env var consumed at orchestrator/cli.py:288-290, defaulting to `max(16, int(os.environ.get('EGG_MAX_CONCURRENT_LONG_POLLS', '64')) + 4)` so the pool is always at least 4 larger than the expected concurrent long-poll count. (2) Waitress already accommodates blocking I/O via its thread pool — NO async worker switch is required; this is *easier* than the gevent path rev 2 proposed. Drop all references to `worker_class`, `gunicorn.conf.py`, `--timeout`, `gevent`, and `eventlet` from plan TASK-4-1 and architect Track 7 — these files/concepts do not exist in this codebase. (3) The dedicated `/healthz` route added by plan TASK-4-2 MUST be MessageStore-free so k8s readiness probes do not contend for request threads; this risk is acute with Waitress where probe + long-poll share the same pool. (4) The `egg_inflight_long_polls` gauge added by plan TASK-4-3 is the primary observability signal for saturation; pair it with a Waitress threads-in-use counter (implement via a decorator that increments on request entry, decrements on exit) so operators can diff the two and localize the stall. (5) Document the thread-count formula in docs/reference/agent-wait-patterns.md with the concrete calculation and a warning that 30+ concurrent long-polls against the default 16 threads will starve short requests within seconds. (6) Memory sizing note: per-thread default stack is ≈8MB; raising to 64 threads adds ≈512MB overhead, well within the current orchestrator memory limit (4Gi per #1885) but worth cross-referencing in the PR description so SRE reviewers don't miss it.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert the new route / CLI so agents fall back to the current 60s `message poll --wait` pattern. Waitress thread-count revert to `threads=16` by deleting the env-var read (or setting `EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS=16` in the ConfigMap). Pre-change baseline restored with no data loss. If Waitress is already starving at the 60s cap under the current code, the deeper problem pre-exists this issue and is out of scope.
risks.human_review_reason: Deployment-config risk crosses into the SRE team's territory. Reviewer should confirm the plan names Waitress thread-count as a first-class task (not Gunicorn — which does not exist in the codebase), and verify the EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS default formula lines up with the expected agent-per-pipeline peak.

risks.title: HTTP_PROXY (Squid) timeout coupling is image-baked; NO ConfigMap affordance for operators
risks.description: Verified at gateway/squid.conf:135-137 — Squid's timeouts are hardcoded: `connect_timeout 30 seconds`, `read_timeout 60 seconds`, `request_timeout 60 seconds`. These directives are NOT exposed via k8s ConfigMap, env var, or entrypoint templating. Checking k8s/base/gateway-deployment.yaml confirms only `PROXY_PORT=3129`, `GATEWAY_PORT`, `HEALTH_PORT`, and `GATEWAY_THREADS=32` are surfaced — no Squid-timeout knob. Rev 2's mitigation ('raise the Squid ConfigMap key') cannot be satisfied by any operator because no such key exists. The same ambiguity infects plan TASK-2-3's startup warning, which currently says 'naming the gateway Squid ConfigMap key the operator must also raise' — that key does not exist. Raising `EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT` beyond 60s today causes Squid to close the connection mid-read, producing spurious 504 Gateway Timeout responses indistinguishable from a real orchestrator hang.
affected_components: orchestrator/routes/messages.py:165 — wait cap read from env
k8s/base/gateway-deployment.yaml — no Squid-timeout env var or ConfigMap key today
gateway/ entrypoint script (if one exists; otherwise a new one that templates squid.conf)
docs/reference/orchestrator-cli.md — current doc location for env vars
risks.mitigation:
Pick exactly ONE of two paths and commit in this PR:

**Path A — runtime knob (recommended if future tuning is expected):** (1) Add a new ConfigMap key (e.g. `gateway-squid-config: "read_timeout=<N> seconds\nrequest_timeout=<N> seconds"`) OR individual env vars (`SQUID_READ_TIMEOUT`, `SQUID_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`). (2) Modify the gateway container entrypoint (write one if absent) to template these values into `squid.conf` at container start via `envsubst` or a simple `sed`. (3) Plan TASK-2-3's startup warning at the orchestrator side checks `EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT` against the env-var-named key (which is now a real knob). (4) Document the linkage: raising `EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT` requires raising the new Squid env vars in the same ConfigMap change.

**Path B — image-rebuild-only (recommended if we want to ship the smaller change):** (1) Introduce a constant `_SQUID_READ_TIMEOUT_HARDCODED = 60` in the orchestrator (matching squid.conf:136). (2) At orchestrator startup, if `EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT > _SQUID_READ_TIMEOUT_HARDCODED`, REFUSE to boot with a fatal error message naming gateway/squid.conf and explaining that a gateway image rebuild is required. (3) The integration test in plan TASK-8-3 asserts the refusal-to-boot, not just a 504. (4) Document the coupling in agent-wait-patterns.md as 'for now, 60s is a hard cap; raising it requires a gateway image rebuild — file an issue to add runtime knob (Path A) if sustained higher-than-60s waits are needed.'

Path B is smaller and safer for this PR; Path A is future-proofing. The reviewer NACK insists that rev 2's 'document it in a runbook' is insufficient — either path's code-level gate IS sufficient. Additionally: (5) DEP-3 status must reflect the chosen path (rev 3 keeps the current 'no affordance' wording because neither A nor B is committed yet; once the plan phase picks one, DEP-3 updates to 'ConfigMap knob present' or 'code-level cap enforced').
risks.rollback_plan: Path A rollback: revert the ConfigMap key + entrypoint template; Squid reverts to its hardcoded defaults; operators who were relying on the raise must accept 504s again. Path B rollback: revert the refusal-to-boot check; operators can once again misconfigure the cap but the failure mode is still a 504 at runtime (not a hang). Neither rollback affects data.
risks.human_review_reason: Cross-component config coupling is exactly the class of bug that passes CI and fails in prod. Reviewer must choose Path A vs Path B; 'document in runbook' alone (rev 2 wording) is insufficient and the reviewer has NACK'd it.

risks.title: In-memory store condition-variable blocking + MessageStore.clear() at phase transitions can block threads forever
risks.description: Decision-4 resolves to implement true blocking via a condition variable on the in-memory MessageStore (orchestrator/message_store.py:70-168). This is load-bearing for local development per Q2. However, MessageStore.clear() is called at phase transitions (line 160-168) to wipe per-pipeline messages. If a thread is waiting on a condition variable when clear() runs, the thread must be: (a) woken up with notify_all(), (b) observe that its pipeline's list is gone, and (c) return an empty result (or a 'stream closed' signal) instead of continuing to wait. A naive implementation that only notifies on add_message() will leave a blocked thread hanging until its next HTTP-level timeout, producing a zombie socket per phase transition.
affected_components: phase-transition call site: typically orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py or orchestrator/concurrent_executor.py
risks.mitigation: (1) Plan task must specify the condition variable is per-pipeline, not global, so one pipeline's clear() does not wake threads for unrelated pipelines. (2) clear() MUST call `cv.notify_all()` after popping the list and before returning; add a comment referencing this risk. (3) The blocking read loop must check `pipeline_id in self._messages` after each wake-up — if gone, return empty list. (4) Unit tests: (a) thread blocks on get_messages(wait=30), clear() fires, thread returns empty within 100ms; (b) thread blocks on get_messages(wait=30), pipeline never transitions, thread returns at wait timeout; (c) two threads block on same pipeline, add_message() fires, both wake up and return the new message. (5) Also close out the long-discussed in-memory silent-fallback at routes/messages.py:181-184 — with condition-variable blocking in place, the `try/except TypeError` fallback can be removed, making the non-blocking CI environment fail loudly instead of silently.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert the condition variable changes; the try/except at routes/messages.py:181-184 still catches the un-supported wait and returns immediately. Behavior degrades to pre-issue semantics. Local-dev agents will still run — just less efficiently.
risks.human_review_reason: Concurrency primitives are easy to get subtly wrong. A reviewer should spot-check the condition-variable semantics against the clear() call path — specifically, does clear() hold the lock while notifying, and can the wake-up observe the cleared state?

risks.title: consensus_wrapper.py Redis coupling breaks local-dev Docker deploys without Redis
risks.description: orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py is currently a pure shell wrapper with no language-runtime dependency beyond `python3 -c "..."` for JSON parsing. It polls `egg-orch pipeline status --json` every 30s for up to MAX_READY_POLLS iterations (lines 322-355). Decision-8 replaces this with 'a long XREAD BLOCK or SSE listener tied to is_complete'. Two options: (a) XREAD BLOCK — introduces a Redis client dependency in the consensus_wrapper, but per Q2, 'local deploys run without Redis for now'. (b) SSE listener — reuses orchestrator/sse.py which is already hot at HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL=15s (sse.py:41). The wrapper would need `curl --no-buffer` or a Python SSE client. Plan Phase 5 / TASK-5-1 locked SSE as the chosen path — curl --no-buffer against the existing EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED at orchestrator/sse.py:67 — which eliminates the Redis-in-local-dev blocker.
affected_components: sandbox image — curl is already bundled; no new runtime dependency
risks.mitigation: (1) Plan Phase 5 / TASK-5-1 LOCKED SSE: `curl --no-buffer https://orchestrator/pipelines/<pid>/events | grep -m1 CONSENSUS_REACHED`. No new runtime dependency; local-dev without Redis keeps working because the SSE endpoint is HTTP, not Redis. (2) If a future implementer revisits and picks XREAD, the wrapper MUST fall back to the current shell sleep loop when Redis is unreachable; fail hard only in explicit `EGG_MESSAGE_STORE_BACKEND=redis` mode. (3) Add a sandbox/tests test that validates the wrapper script reaches is_complete within the expected time under the SSE primitive. (4) Document in the wrapper shebang comment that SSE is in use and that replacement with Redis requires a local-dev fallback.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert to the existing shell sleep loop. No data impact. Consensus detection degrades from event-driven to 30s-poll, which is the current baseline.

risks.title: Python SIGTERM handling on long SSE connections — verify curl --no-buffer honors signals cleanly
risks.description: Rev 2 entertained XREAD BLOCK and SSE alternatives; plan Phase 5 / TASK-5-1 has LOCKED the SSE path (curl --no-buffer against EventType.CONSENSUS_REACHED at orchestrator/sse.py:67). With SSE chosen, the SIGTERM concern narrows: does `curl --no-buffer` honor SIGTERM cleanly and close the socket within the k8s terminationGracePeriodSeconds (default 30s)? Curl's standard behavior is to close the socket and exit on SIGTERM, but this must be verified under the specific consensus_wrapper invocation pattern (piped through grep/awk, running under a sandbox tini/init).
risks.mitigation: (1) Sandbox test pointer: plan TASK-5-1 acceptance criteria MUST include a test at `sandbox/tests/test_consensus_wrapper_sigterm.py` (or equivalent) that: spawns the wrapper, waits until the curl SSE connection is established (observable via `ss -tn` or a short delay), sends SIGTERM, asserts the wrapper exits within `terminationGracePeriodSeconds - 5` (25s for a default 30s grace), and asserts `exit 0` (since consensus-not-yet-reached + SIGTERM is a clean shutdown, not a failure). (2) Verify the wrapper's shell pipeline forwards SIGTERM correctly: `curl | grep -m1 ...` — grep exits when curl exits. If a subshell or backgrounded curl is used, SIGTERM delivery needs `trap` handling. (3) Document the terminationGracePeriodSeconds assumption in the wrapper so a future k8s manifest edit that shrinks the grace period does not silently regress. (4) No XREAD-BLOCK-specific SIGTERM handling is needed — that path was withdrawn by plan TASK-5-1.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert to shell sleep loop — shell `sleep` naturally exits on SIGTERM. The fix's benefit (faster consensus detection) is lost; no correctness regression.

risks.title: Prompt-only 'Do NOT' regression guard is cheap to erase
risks.description: Decision-7 is to add explicit 'Don'ts' to the prompt preamble in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py: 'Do NOT use for-loops to wrap message poll; do NOT call sleep N to wait; rely on --wait blocking semantics'. This is a prompt-only fix. Future prompt edits can remove or water down the language without tripping any guard. Prompt-regression tests in orchestrator/tests/test_pipeline_prompts.py lock in the current 'STAY ALIVE' structure but do NOT yet assert the absence of 'sleep ' or 'for i in' patterns in the rendered prompt — so an agent-facing regression can slip through green tests.
risks.mitigation: (1) Add a locked-in test in test_pipeline_prompts.py that asserts the rendered prompt for every role contains the literal strings 'Do NOT' and 'rely on --wait blocking semantics'. (2) Add a negative-assertion test that the rendered prompt does NOT contain 'Keep polling' or 'for i in' (to catch accidental re-introduction). (3) Mirror the assertions against sandbox/agent-config/rules/mission.md via a parametrized test. (4) Add a code comment at the prompt definition pointing at the tests so future editors see the coupling. (5) Decision-7 explicitly rejected gateway-level bash enforcement, so the prompt tests ARE the final line of defense.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert prompt changes — the 'Do NOT' lines are additive. Tests revert with them. Agents fall back to the existing prompt shape.

risks.title: Single recommended idiom exit-code contract is underspecified
risks.description: Q5 resolution is to ship the single idiom `while true; do egg-orch message wait --for <TYPE> || break; done` and ban alternatives. The `|| break` semantics mean any non-zero exit breaks the loop. If `egg-orch message wait` exits non-zero on transient network blips, orchestrator 503s, or JSON parse errors (in addition to 'matched message' and 'timeout'), the loop breaks prematurely and the agent goes silent. Conversely, if the command exits 0 on timeout, the loop spins forever — burning the exact resources the issue set out to reclaim. Plan TASK-2-2 RESOLVED this by codifying 0=matched / 1=timeout / 2=transient / 3=permanent and TASK-2-4 wraps it in `egg-orch message wait-loop --for TYPE` that encodes the correct retry behavior.
risks.mitigation: (1) RESOLVED by plan TASK-2-2 (exit-code contract codified) and TASK-2-4 (wait-loop meta-command). (2) Document the contract in the CLI --help output AND agent-wait-patterns.md. (3) The recommended idiom the prompt SHOWS is `egg-orch message wait-loop --for TYPE` not the raw `while ... || break` form — keep the decision-tree in the wrapper so the prompt doesn't leak exit-code knowledge. (4) Unit test every exit-code path explicitly (plan TASK-2-2 acceptance criteria).
risks.rollback_plan: Fall back to the current 60s `egg-orch message poll --wait 60` wrapped in a single `while true` — matches the current prompt intent even without the new primitive.

risks.title: Test-suite churn from removing QUESTION is broader than plan phase may anticipate
risks.description: grep shows QUESTION used in at least orchestrator/tests/test_brc_history.py (4 assertions), orchestrator/tests/test_concurrent_integration.py (2 assertions), gateway/tests/test_checkpoint_inter_agent.py (2 assertions), plus the schema-level enum. Removing QUESTION requires touching all of these. A partial update where BRC_HISTORY_TYPES still includes QUESTION but MessageType enum doesn't will cause runtime errors on checkpoint serialization. Same hazard in reverse for docs.
risks.mitigation: (1) Plan phase must enumerate every QUESTION reference as a named task (rg 'QUESTION' --type py --type md) and include the output in the plan doc. (2) Commit ordering: (a) drop QUESTION from the reviewer prompt preamble, (b) update all tests to not rely on QUESTION, (c) remove QUESTION from BRC_HISTORY_TYPES, (d) remove from MessageType enum. Each stage must keep tests green. (3) Single-PR strategy vs incremental: if done in one PR, run full test suite before pushing; if incremental, stage behind a feature-flag env var that hides QUESTION from the enum when set.

risks.title: In-flight pipelines at deploy time continue the old sleep/poll shape
risks.description: When the orchestrator rolls out the new prompt + CLI, pipelines already mid-flight have agents that were spawned with the OLD prompt and don't have the new `message wait` CLI (it ships in the sandbox image, which is respun per-pipeline). Those agents continue the old polling shape until they respawn or the pipeline completes. No functional break, but the first ~24-48 hours after deploy still contain sleep/poll behavior. This is a non-risk if rollout is expected; it's only a bug if someone claims 'deploy fixed everything'.
risks.mitigation: (1) Document in the PR body / docs that the fix applies to NEW pipelines only. (2) If urgency is high, the overseer can manually terminate long-running stale pipelines and let them respawn with the new image. (3) Add a log at orchestrator boot that emits the BRC-preamble version (a monotonically increasing integer) so post-deploy validation can confirm new prompts are flowing.
risks.rollback_plan: No rollback needed — deploy is additive; old pipelines finish on old semantics.

risks.title: Scope creep — 9+ independent artifacts in one implement phase
risks.description: The decision-1 resolution (all five items) plus HEARTBEAT addition plus the Waitress-threads correction yields at least 10 distinct artifacts in the implement phase: (a) prompt preamble edit; (b) new CLI subcommand + wait-loop wrapper; (c) new HTTP route + Redis+in-memory blocking; (d) new env var; (e) new HEARTBEAT type + health_monitor wiring; (f) QUESTION removal across prompt/tests/docs; (g) consensus_wrapper SSE replacement; (h) agent-wait-patterns.md; (i) mission.md edit; (j) Waitress thread-count env var + /healthz + inflight gauge. Large, cross-cutting PR surface. Reviewer fatigue increases the chance of a subtle risk (RISK-1, RISK-2, RISK-3, RISK-4, or RISK-5) slipping through.
risks.mitigation: (1) task_planner should decompose into parallel tracks (per scope-summary in the contract) so tracks can land independently: Track A (prompts + docs, low-risk, land first); Track B (new CLI + route + blocking, core change); Track C (HEARTBEAT + health_monitor wiring, cross-subsystem); Track D (QUESTION removal, test churn); Track E (Waitress threads + /healthz + gauge, deployment). (2) Each track should be a separate commit series on the same implement PR with clear commit messages, OR split across multiple implement-phase iterations if the pipeline supports it. (3) Review checklist should call out the four high-severity risks by name so no reviewer misses them. (4) If time-boxed, SHIP tracks A + B + C + E first; DEFER track D (QUESTION removal) to a follow-up issue — this keeps the reviewer affordance intact while unblocking the core wait-primitive work.

areas_needing_human_review: RISK-1 — confirm decision-5 (remove QUESTION) is still intended given QUESTION is in the reviewer prompt preamble and BRC_HISTORY_TYPES (not just test fixtures as the refine phase claimed).

RISK-2 — verify the plan wires health_monitor to subscribe to both PROGRESS-heartbeat AND HEARTBEAT message-bus events; otherwise Tier 1 alerts fire on agents that are reporting state correctly via the new channel. Also: decide whether to land the HEARTBEAT rate-limit (architect TD-3) in this PR or explicitly defer as residual.
RISK-3 — confirm the plan renames WSGI-config work from Gunicorn/gevent to Waitress thread-tuning (orchestrator/cli.py:288-290). The rev 2 phrasing was factually incorrect.
RISK-4 — confirm the plan picks Path A (ConfigMap + entrypoint template) or Path B (hardcoded cap + refusal-to-boot). Rev 2 suggested a runbook note; reviewer NACK'd that as insufficient.
RISK-5 — spot-check the condition-variable design on the in-memory MessageStore against clear() at phase transitions; ensure blocked threads wake up and return cleanly.

security_posture_summary.before: QUESTION messages unreplied-to; consensus_confirmed retry-loop pollution (fixed by #1896 before this issue). No new attack surface.
security_posture_summary.after: New `egg-orch message wait` CLI route uses existing session auth — no new mutating surface. HEARTBEAT message type is broadcast-only from each agent to the bus, same trust model as PROGRESS. New env var EGG_MESSAGE_POLL_MAX_WAIT is read at orchestrator boot; its value is non-secret. New env var EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS read at orchestrator boot; non-secret. No new secrets, no new cross-boundary mutation paths.
security_posture_summary.net_change: Neutral — no security regressions, no new auth surfaces. Two adjacent considerations worth naming: (a) long-lived connections increase the opportunity window for a compromised agent to exfiltrate data through long-polled bus payloads, but the message content is not broader than what the agent can already read via short-polling. (b) `egg-orch message wait --for HEARTBEAT` is observable by a compromised reviewer agent and exposes other roles' state-transition pattern as a side channel (WORKING → WAITING_ON_ROLE → PROPOSED → IDLE transitions are visible); however the existing message bus already exposes the same data via short-polling of CONSENSUS_PROPOSE / CONSENSUS_ACK events, so net change is still neutral.

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: The change is additive plus one subtract (QUESTION). Each artifact can be reverted independently. If a rollback is required under load, revert in this order: (1) consensus_wrapper SSE listener → shell sleep loop (preserves consensus detection with 30s lag); (2) new CLI + route (agents fall back to `egg-orch message poll --wait 60` — already in prompt); (3) Waitress thread-count env var → hardcoded 16 (matches pre-change baseline); (4) prompt Don'ts (agents regain old wording); (5) HEARTBEAT type + health_monitor wiring (Tier 1 falls back to PROGRESS-heartbeat path, which was never removed); (6) QUESTION removal — only rollback if a reviewer workflow actually broke. Each step is independent and independently safe.

partial_rollback_options.cli_only: Revert the `egg-orch message wait` CLI + route; keep the prompt Don'ts and docs. Agents fall back to `message poll --wait` and the Don'ts still guide them away from for-loop wrappers.
partial_rollback_options.heartbeat_only: Revert HEARTBEAT type + health_monitor subscription; keep the CLI + prompt. Tier 1 reverts to PROGRESS-heartbeat path. Agents that already learned the new message type gracefully degrade (unknown message types are ignored).
partial_rollback_options.question_only: Revert QUESTION removal (restore enum + prompt text + tests). Zero impact on the wait-primitive work.
partial_rollback_options.waitress_threads_only: Revert EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS env var read; hardcode back to 16. Saturation risk returns if new CLI is in use, but short-request path still works.

rollback_plan.monitoring_post_deploy: Post-deploy, watch: (a) overseer alert rate (should drop — fewer 'silent agent' nudges); (b) p50 / p95 consensus turn-around time (should drop — agents react to ACKs/NACKs in seconds); (c) Waitress threads-in-use gauge + egg_inflight_long_polls (should NOT both approach EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS — if they do, see RISK-3); (d) 504 rate on GET /api/v1/pipelines/<id>/messages (should be zero — if not, see RISK-4); (e) heartbeat_timeout alert rate on agents that have adopted HEARTBEAT (should be zero — if not, see RISK-2); (f) post-boot orchestrator logs MUST include the BRC-preamble version integer and the resolved EGG_ORCH_WAITRESS_THREADS value so operators can confirm the new config flowed.
